parts.problem_md:
A parallel plate capacitor** **X of capacitance 300 μF is fully charged to a potential difference of 8 V.

Calculate the charge stored by X when it is fully charged.
parts.solution_md:
List the known quantities:

- Capacitance, *C* = 300 μF = 300 × 10<sup>­–6</sup> F
- Potential difference, *V* = 8 V

Rearrange the equation for capacitance to calculate the charge stored:

- $C=\frac{Q}{V}$
- So, the charge stored *Q* = *CV ***[1 mark]**

Substitute in the values:

- *Q* = (300 × 10<sup>–6</sup>) × 8 **[1 mark]**
- *Q* = 2.4 × 10<sup>–3</sup> C **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

A parallel plate capacitor X of capacitance 300 μF is fully charged to a potential difference of 8 V.

A parallel plate capacitor Y is placed in series with the parallel plate capacitor X. Capacitor Y has a capacitance of 200 µF.

Calculate the combined capacitance of capacitors X and Y in this arrangement.
parts.solution_md:
List the known quantities:

- Capacitance of capacitor X, *C*<sub>*X*</sub>* *= 300 µF
- Capacitance of capacitor Y, *C*<sub>*Y*</sub>* *= 200 µF

State the relationship between the capacitance of capacitors in series:

- $\frac{1}{C_{T}}=\frac{1}{C_{X}}+\frac{1}{C_{Y}}$ **[1 mark]**

Substitute the known quantities into the equation:

- $\frac{1}{C_{T}}=\frac{1}{300}+\frac{1}{200}$ **[1 mark]**

Rearrange the equation to make total capacitance, *C*<sub>*T*</sub>  the subject:

- $\frac{1}{C_{T}}=\frac{1}{120}$
- $120=C_{T}$
- So, $C_{T}=120$ µF** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

parts.problem_md: Define the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor.
parts.solution_md:
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is:

- The ratio of the charge stored to potential (difference) **OR** the charge stored per unit potential (difference); ** [1 mark]**
- Where the charge is the magnitude of the charge on one plate **AND** the potential difference is across the two plates;** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

parts.solution_md:
The functions of capacitors connected in electrical circuits are:

[1]

Consider mathematically the combination of capacitors and their combined capacitance:

List the known quantities:

- Capacitance of each capacitor, *C *= 24 μF

Two capacitors in series with one in parallel:

- `C space equals space open parentheses fraction numerator 1 over denominator 1 over 24 space plus space 1 over 24 end fraction close parentheses space plus space 24 space equals space 36 space straight mu straight F`

Two capacitors in parallel with one in series:

parts.problem_md:
Three capacitors, each of capacitance 27 μF, are connected as shown in Fig. 1.1.

capacitance = ..................................... μF
parts.solution_md:
Calculate the total capacitance between points P and Q:

List the known quantities:

- Capacitance of each capacitor, *C *= 27 μF

Calculate the capacitance of the parallel combination, *C*<sub>*P*</sub>:

- $C_{P}=C+C$
- $C_{P}=27+27$
- $C_{P}=54\mathrm{μF}$ **[1 mark]**

Calculate the capacitance of the series combination, *C*<sub>*S*</sub>:

**[Total: 2 marks]**

> *You do not need to convert the capacitance from μF into F because the final answer is required in μF.*

**Extract:**

Three capacitors, each of capacitance 27 μF, are connected as shown in Fig. 1.1. [Fig 1.1: one 27 μF capacitor in series with a parallel combination of two 27 μF capacitors, between points P and Q]. From part (a): Capacitance of each capacitor, C = 27 × 10^−6 F; Capacitance across the parallel combination, C_P = 54 × 10^−6 F; total series capacitance = 18 μF.

The maximum safe potential difference that can be applied across any one capacitor is 4 V.

Determine the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied between points P and Q.

potential difference = ...................................... V
parts.solution_md:
Determine the maximum safe potential difference that can be applied between points P and Q:

List the known quantities:

- Max p.d. across each capacitor = 4 V
- Capacitance of each capacitor, *C *= 27 × 10<sup>−6</sup> F (From part (a))
- Capacitance across the parallel combination, *C*<sub>*P*</sub> = 54 × 10<sup>−6</sup> F (From part (a))

Calculate the safe p.d. across the parallel combination:

- For components in series, the charge across each component is the same

  - Consider the single capacitor as component 1 and the parallel combination as component 2 in the circuit
  - Hence, *Q*<sub>*1*</sub> = *Q*<sub>*2*</sub>
- The total charge from P to Q = charge across the single capacitor

  - $Q_{1}=C_{1}V_{max}$
  - `Q subscript 1 space equals space open parentheses 27 space cross times space 10 to the power of negative 6 end exponent close parentheses space cross times space 4`
  - $Q_{1}=1.08\times10^{-4}C$
- So, the p.d. across the parallel combination is:

  - `V subscript 2 space equals space Q subscript 2 over C subscript P space equals space fraction numerator open parentheses 1.08 space cross times space 10 to the power of negative 4 end exponent close parentheses over denominator open parentheses 54 space cross times space 10 to the power of negative 6 end exponent close parentheses end fraction space equals space 2 space straight V` **[1 mark]**

Calculate the p.d. across the series combination:

- p.d. in series combination = p.d. in parallel + p.d. across single
- p.d. in series combination = 2 + 4 = 6 V **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**
